direction: 2D Ising Monte Carlo with a phase classifier. Generate spin configurations for L = 16, 24, 32 with a vectorised checkerboard Metropolis or Wolff sampler in NumPy at 40 temperatures in [1.5, 3.5] (200 decorrelated samples each). Train logistic regression, an MLP and a small CNN on temperatures far from Tc, read Tc from the 0.5 crossing of the output, and do a finite-size scaling collapse. Compare with PCA and learning-by-confusion; measure Tc error against 2 / ln(1 + sqrt(2)). Keep it a small CPU study with reimplemented baselines, at least 5 seeds where cheap, and report negative or mixed results plainly.

decisions.decision: No novel method claimed: controlled comparison. Sampler: Swendsen-Wang cluster (batched, SciPy connected components) instead of Wolff because it vectorises over all temperatures and chains; checkerboard Metropolis is implemented and used to cross-check energies against Onsager.

Single run = system x seed over all three L (data regenerated from seed, cached). 4 independent chains x 50 samples per T: chains 0-2 train, chain 3 test, so the output curve is always evaluated on unseen chains. Hyperparameters fixed a priori (not tuned on Tc error); pilot on seed 100 used only to check run time.

10 seeds (cheap). Estimators fixed before main runs: supervised/ordered-prob 0.5 first downward crossing; PCA peak of Var|PC1| in [1.9,3.1] + collapse of mean|PC1|/max; confusion peak of accuracy in [1.9,3.1]; reference susceptibility peak and Binder collapse. Collapse: grid Tc in [2.0,2.6], nu in [0.5,2.0], window |T-Tc|<=0.6.
